decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY captures literal terminal extraction but omits that the approved derivation source is the attached Option 2 Hero V rather than the revised presentation version.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Thank you for assembling the family. Bringing the capital V, lowercase v, and É accent together is exactly the next step we needed, and I think it confirms that we are now developing an architectural language rather than refining a single letter.

It also made one point very clear to me. The hero V is still Option 2 from the previous round, which I’m attaching here as a reference. That silhouette remains the strongest foundation in my view, and I’d like us to continue constructing the system from that version instead of using the revised hero V shown in this presentation.

Seeing the family together led to another important realization: I don’t want the É accent merely to take inspiration from the hero V. I want it to be, literally, the termination of the hero V.

The relationship I’m imagining is that you could remove the final portion of the hero V's right arm, lift it from the letter, and position it over the É. Those should be the exact same gesture. I believe that degree of consistency is what will make the identity feel genuinely proprietary.

I’d love to keep refining the system around that principle. Once the gesture is completely unified across the capital V, lowercase v, and É accent, I think we will have created something truly special.

value_updates.derivation_source: The attached Option 2 from the previous round's Hero V geometry rather than the revised Hero V shown in the family presentation.
value_updates.derivation_method: Literal extraction of the terminal section of the approved Hero V's right arm
value_updates.required_correspondence: The É accent must be the exact same gesture as the Hero V terminal rather than a related interpretation.
